summary: Eric David Mortensen specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2003) under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton, also studying under Chongren He, Xiaoxun He, Zhiben He, Xi Aniu, and Xuewen He.

Eric Haruki Swanson works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He has held a post at Loyola Marymount University and served at Stanford University as a Senior Visiting Scholar (attested 2026).
Eric Huntington is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Gary A. Tubb.

Eric J. Sharpe (1933–2000) was a religious studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Hartley Victoria College, the University of Manchester, and Uppsala University, he held posts at Manchester (1966), Lancaster (1970), Uppsala (1978–1981), and Sydney (1977–1996).

Eric M. Greene is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who earned his PhD from UC Berkeley in 2012 under Robert H. Sharf. He held posts as Assistant Professor (attested 2017) and Associate Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2026) at Yale University.

Eric Stephen Goodell specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned master's degrees from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia (attested 2012), where he studied under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner.

Erica Baffelli is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied under Massimo Raveri. She held a post at the University of Otago (attested 2015) and serves as Professor in Japanese Studies at the University of Manchester (attested 2016, 2026).
Erica Biagetti specializes in Indology, linguistics, and computational studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Pavia in 2021, where she also held an academic post.

Erich Frauwallner (1898–1974) was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. Educated at the University of Vienna (1918–1921), he held Vienna posts including director (1938, 1942) and professor (1955–1964), and edited the Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde Süd- und Ostasiens (~1957–1974).

Erich Haenisch (1880–1966) was a Sinologist and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Wilhelm Grube. He held professorships at Göttingen (1925), Leipzig (~1925–1932), Berlin (1932), and Munich (1927–1951).

Erich Heintel (1912–2000) was a philosopher who earned his doctorate (1931–1936) and habilitation (1940) at the University of Vienna. He served Vienna as extraordinary professor (1952) and ordinary professor of philosophy (1960–1982), and joined the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Erich Rudolf Jaensch (1883–1940) was a philosopher. After studying at Breslau, Göttingen (PhD 1905–1908), and Strasbourg, he served as Ordinarius for philosophy at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1912–1913) and as ordinary professor at the University of Marburg from 1913.

Erik Braun is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied at Harvard University under Janet Gyatso, Jonathan Evans, John Okell, and Saw Tun. He held a faculty post at the University of Virginia (attested 2026).

Erik Haarh (1929–1993) was a Tibetologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of Copenhagen (attested 1969). He held positions at the Royal Danish Library (1956, 1962) and served as a department head and theology professor at Aarhus University (1969, 1983).

Erik J. Hammerstrom specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2010) and served as assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).
Erik Pema Kunsang (born 1933) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He has served as director of Rangjung Yeshe Publications and as resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark.

Erik Zürcher (1928–2008) was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Leiden University (~1947–1959), studying under Paul Demiéville, Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak. He served as Director at Leiden University (1961–1993).

Erik-Jan Zürcher (born 1953) is a historian and linguist educated at Leiden University (BA ~1971–1974, PhD ~1977–1984). He held posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1977–1997), the International Institute of Social History (1990–1999, 2008–2012), and Leiden University (1997).

Erling von Mende (born 1940) is a Sinologist who studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, and Bonn, completing his PhD (1964–1969) and habilitation (~1972–1979) at the University of Cologne. He served as Professor of Sinology at the Free University of Berlin (1983–2007).
Ernest Arthur Gardner (1862–1939) was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Gonville and Caius College (~1880–1884). He held an academic post at the University of London from 1924 to 1926.
